name: ARMoR (Alliance for Reducing Microbial Resistance)
summary: Advocates for pull incentives, such as subscription payments, that fund the development of and access to new antimicrobials against drug-resistant infections.

spending.source: https://www.armoramr.org/financials ($226,477 received from September 2023 to March 2025, gifts and consulting fees) and https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/srjXGXhsecmZvpEdq/two-years-of-doing-advocacy-on-antimicrobial-resistance ($17,000 a month of full operations in late 2025, $10,000 in late 2024): ARMoR is a fiscally sponsored project and publishes no accounts; our model's average yearly spending from September 2023 to December 2025, in 2025 prices (85% of the receipts spent by March 2025, then about $13,500 a month), all counted as programme.

lines.label: Advocacy and research for pull incentives for new antibiotics (EU, national, G7), and research commissioned by its clients
lines.source: Our model's average yearly spending from September 2023 to December 2025 (https://www.armoramr.org/financials; https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/HXqzmahbjJwwiX9Si/one-year-of-doing-advocacy-on-antimicrobial-resistance). ARMoR publishes no split by programme: its EU advocacy, national advocacy, G7 work and commissioned research are branches of one model. Its access programme for low- and middle-income countries began in May 2026, after the period.
